preconditions.description: The number of workers is between 1 and 5000, inclusive.
The parameter k is a rational number with a numerator a and denominator b, where both a and b are between 1 and 10^5, inclusive.
The string s represents the job categories of the workers, and its length is equal to the number of workers n.

postconditions.expression: output == [str(c) for c in sorted(set(s) & obtainable_categories)]
postconditions.description: The output is a list of the obtainable job categories sorted in lexicographical order, where each category is represented as a string.

invariants.expression: all(c not in s for c in 'trygub')
invariants.description: The job categories do not contain any of the letters 't', 'r', 'y', 'g', 'u', and 'b', which are not present in the string s.

invariants.expression: all(c in s for c in obtainable_categories)
invariants.description: All obtainable job categories are present in the string s.

invariants.expression: all(k * (max(positions) - min(positions) + 1) <= len(positions) for x in set(s) for positions in [positions for positions, category in enumerate(s) if category == x])
invariants.description: For each job category x, the condition k * (i_m - i_1 + 1) <= m is satisfied for all positions i_1, ..., i_m of workers with job category x.
